paper_id: Rethinking Backdoor Detection Evaluation for Language Models
evidence: We generate backdoored models with three different training intensities.
covering 18 individual comparisons of the three training intensities (2 datasets × 3 triggers × 3 detectors)
We conduct poisoning-based backdoor attacks on two binary classification datasets: SST-2
We calculate the Detection Accuracy (%) on backdoored models as the evaluation metric.
unresolved: n_seeds left null: paper says results are 'averaged attack success rate and clean accuracy' (Tables 1-2) but never states how many runs/seeds/trials were averaged, so no repetition count could be confirmed.

n_models counted as the 4 distinct victim architectures (RoBERTa-Base, RoBERTa-Large, Electra-Base, Llama 3.2 1B); the 3 detectors (PICCOLO, DBS, Meta Classifier) are the objects under evaluation, not additional 'models', and are reflected in n_eval_types/n_baselines instead.

n_baselines set to 0: this is an evaluation/audit paper testing 3 existing detectors rather than proposing a new method compared against baselines, so no comparison method fits the 'baseline' role; the 3 detectors are the evaluated subjects, counted implicitly via the evidence quotes rather than as a baseline count.

n_eval_types = 5 combines the 3 quantitative metrics (Detection Accuracy, Attack Success Rate, Clean Accuracy) with 2 qualitative analysis types (loss-contour visualization, t-SNE feature visualization) used in the case study; if only quantitative metrics count, the true figure is 3.
reports_variability = 'none': no error bars, standard deviations, or confidence intervals appear anywhere in the main text, tables, or appendix tables (1-7).
